rules: table: something writes it (a POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE or INTERNAL route, or a server:* declaration). A GET's query parameters are not writers.
view: read only, worked out on read from the tables named in 'of'. No table of its own.
config: price book, settings, catalogues and templates that staff change; a table seeded with reference rows where a declaration gives them.
document: stored whole as validated JSON. 'host' names the model and column that hold it.
not-stored: kept in the web app by ruling.

Columns of a table: every field its declaration lists, plus every registry field that a write route or a server:* declaration writes, plus (for a resource with no declaration) every registry field. A registry field that is a read-side join or a derived display value of a declared resource stays in the contract only.
A dotted field (content.cover) lives inside its root column as JSON. A field whose name is reader prose, not a name, is left out.

Storage nullability: a declared field keeps its declared nullability; a screen-only field is nullable in storage (no writer guarantees it at insert), while the contract keeps the registry's nullability.
Relations: one foreign key per dep-graph.json edge between two stored models.

Ownership: a stored resource that the dep-graph leaves without an owner but whose routes are scoped to the signed-in account (/v1/me, /v1/feed, /v1/studio, /v1/creator) or to the member's business (/v1/business) gets one foreign key to Account or Business ('owner'), because conventions.md (Who can do what) asks for the ownership check. Listed per resource.
An admin action's reason and action are written to the audit row (DEC-125), not to the subject, unless a declaration lists them as fields.

Erase (Q9): 'erase' names every column holding personal data with rule blank (set to null or '' when the account is erased) or keep (with the reason). test/schema/schema.rulings.spec.ts checks each named column exists.
Indexes (INT-1): 'indexes' lists extra indexes a ruling asks for, each a list of columns.
U7 (INT-1): a staff account can never be deleted at the database (trigger staff_account_no_delete); a removed member stays, status removed (S3).
Refs on delete (INT-2): 'refOnDelete' names the delete rule of one reference column (Cascade, Restrict, SetNull); the model's 'onDelete' is the default.
Join tables (INT-2, Y5): top-level 'joinTables' adds tables that are no registry resource (storage only, no contract shape), each with columns, refs, refOnDelete, unique.

X23 (INT-2): every *FileId column is a uuid with a real foreign key to stored_file; a file still named by a row cannot be deleted (Restrict), its signed reads and screening results go with it (Cascade). B09's link triggers are dropped.

AA2 (INT-2): every String, String[] and Json column of a table with an owner key (accountId, ownerAccountId, businessId or creatorId to Account, Business or Creator), and of Account, has an erase rule (blank or keep with why); scripts/check-contracts.mjs fails when one has none. Id columns (id, *Id) are keys, not text.

INT-4 (GG1, LL1): purchase_grant, wish_reaction, wish_favourite, link_hit and pass_draw are models (join tables, storage only, no contract shape); WishOpen gains the columns the receiver's link wrote by SQL. Legacy Wish columns that no route writes any more (GG7) are kept with 'keep' so no row loses data.

kind.why: what the line grants, no person

detail.why: what was granted (counts, days, ticket names); money and entitlement record, names no person

WishReaction.reason: LL1: one reaction per opening session of a wish, changeable; written by SQL from the receiver's link, counted for the owner

reaction.why: a short reaction word from a receiver who has no account

WishFavourite.reason: LL1: the photo positions an opening session marked, one set per session of a wish; written by SQL from the receiver's link

LinkHit.reason: LL1, LL4: the public link's limits counted in the database: a bucket, a key (a hash of the address, never the address) and the time; old rows are removed by a timed job

key.why: a hash; the address cannot be got back

PassDraw.reason: GG3, GG5: a wish or an upgrade drawn from an account's Pass for one wish; the unique key keeps a wish from drawing twice, and the draw is made in the same transaction as the counter

InvoiceCounter.reason: OO4 (B17): the invoice number counter, one row (id 1), taken with a row lock inside the settle transaction so numbers run in order with no gaps; a config table, no contract shape

InvoiceLink.reason: OO4 (B17): what ties an invoice to the payment it came from, its period and whether a refund voided it; one row per invoice

ModerationDecision.reason: QQ6 (B13): the staff reason for one decision (a publish request or a report), read back by the owner (decline) and the staff queues; the subject is one of two tables, so no foreign key

subject.why: the kind of record decided (publish_request or report), no person

reason.why: the staff reason for a decision on a record; it names no account and is read by the owner of a declined request while the request exists

ReportHit.reason: QQ6 (B13): the report limit per address, counted in the database: a key (an HMAC of the address, never the address) and the time

key.why: a keyed hash of the address, never the address: nothing to blank

TakeDownCode.reason: QQ6 (B13): 'This is me, take it down': the code mailed to the address before a report counts; short lived, removed once used or expired

email.why: the reporter's address, not an account's; removed by the take-down flow once the code is used or expired

codeHash.why: a hash of a short-lived code, no person

ConciergeOrderExt.reason: CA2 (B19): a Concierge order's own price (kobo, fixed when it is placed), its payment and its times

ConciergeOrderWish.reason: CA2 (B19): the wishes a maker delivered for an order (a wish is delivered under one order only)

EmailSuppression.reason: YY3 (B20): an address that complained: no more email goes to it; keyed by the address's keyed hash

hash.why: a keyed hash of the address (HMAC), never the address: nothing to blank

SupportIntakeCount.reason: YY3 (B20): contact-page and inbound-mail intake: one row per (kind, key, UTC day), raised by one conditional statement so two requests at once cannot both pass the last place

key.why: a keyed hash of the address or network, never the address: nothing to blank

PayoutDetail.reason: WW4 (B16): what the payout table has no column for: when it was handed to the provider and when it was paid, why it failed, the staff note of a manual paid, and the short lease that keeps two runs from sending one payout at once

note.why: a staff note on a money record, names no person

RoyaltyReversal.reason: WW4 (B16): the negative row of a refunded payment's royalty: one row per accrual, never a delete of the accrual

StyleSubmissionSnapshot.reason: XX4 (B15): the frozen draft of each submission (T-63: the checks and the reviewer read the snapshot, never the live draft); accountId is a plain id (no relation, so the table is not an owned table of the erase gate)

document.why: the creator's own style work: deleted with a submission that never went live, kept for one that did (T-62), by StudioErasure

used.why: which review was spent (plan or extra), not personal

RevealAccess.reason: EA1 (B18): what a reveal link holds beyond reveal_link: its code, passcode, wrong tries, end, switched off, the chosen files; the one-per-client-wish rule is a partial unique index kept in SQL

code.why: the link's own code, a secret that ends with the link (switched off or past its end)

fileIds.why: ids of stored files, which the erase of a business's files removes

passcodeHash.why: a hash of the passcode the business chose; the link is switched off by an erase

RevealVisit.reason: EA1 (B18): one row per visit of a reveal link, holding a keyed hash of the visitor and never the visitor (the table is named reveal_play)

visit.why: a keyed hash of one visit, never the visitor: nothing to blank

RevealSend.reason: EA1 (B18): the sends of a reveal that carried an Idempotency-Key, so a repeat sends nothing twice

key.why: the caller's Idempotency-Key, a random string, no person

VaultPeak.reason: EA1 (B18): the most a business's Vault held in a month, in bytes (the peak the monthly billing reads)

WishStart.reason: HM3 (DEC-214): the Idempotency-Key a person started a wish with and the draft it answered, so the same key answers the same draft whatever happened to the draft since

key.why: a random request key the web made, no person; it only lets a repeated start find its draft

WishGather.reason: HS1: the gather link a wish's owner gives friends to add a voice (one per wish; its own slug, never the wish's link)

slug.why: a random link name, no person

WishGatherVoice.reason: HS1: who a friend's voice note is from (the friend's first name)
